note: Descale EXTRA rules — Linux. Additional cleanup rules beyond the built-in per-OS set (AI model caches, dev-tool caches, Flatpak/Docker pruning), translated from the Leftover project's public catalog. Every rule cites a 'source' doc page and a 'comeback' line (how the content regenerates). These load on top of wpurge-linux-rules.json; each can be switched off under ⚙️ Settings without editing this file. AI rules are review-tier: models are huge re-downloads, so they are never pre-selected.

rules.title: Ollama — pulled models
rules.description: Models you pulled with Ollama (~/.ollama/models). They are re-downloadable but can be many GB each, so this is never pre-selected. Skipped while Ollama is running.
rules.comeback: Pull any model again with: ollama pull <model>. To remove just one instead of everything, use: ollama rm <model>

rules.title: Hugging Face — model cache
rules.description: Model weights and files downloaded from the Hugging Face Hub by transformers, diffusers and other libraries (~/.cache/huggingface/hub).
rules.comeback: Downloaded again the next time code loads the model (as long as it is still on the Hub).

rules.title: Hugging Face — datasets cache
rules.description: Datasets downloaded and processed by the datasets library (~/.cache/huggingface/datasets).
rules.comeback: Downloaded and processed again the next time code loads the dataset.

rules.title: LM Studio — model library
rules.description: Models in LM Studio's library (~/.lmstudio/models, ~/.cache/lm-studio/models). Some may have been imported from your own files rather than downloaded, so they cannot be promised to come back. Skipped while LM Studio is running.
rules.comeback: Models downloaded inside LM Studio can be downloaded again from its Discover tab.

rules.title: PyTorch — Hub cache
rules.description: Models and weights downloaded through torch.hub and torchvision (~/.cache/torch).
rules.comeback: Downloaded again the next time code loads them.

rules.title: Whisper — models
rules.description: Speech recognition models downloaded by OpenAI's Whisper package (~/.cache/whisper).
rules.comeback: Downloaded again the first time you load a model.

rules.title: llama.cpp — downloaded models
rules.description: Models llama.cpp downloaded with -hf or --hf-repo (~/.cache/llama.cpp). Newer versions use the Hugging Face cache instead.
rules.comeback: llama.cpp downloads a model again the next time you run it with -hf. Check that nothing points at these files by path first.

rules.title: GPT4All — models and LocalDocs
rules.description: Models the GPT4All app downloaded, and its LocalDocs index (~/.local/share/nomic.ai/GPT4All).
rules.comeback: Remove models from inside GPT4All, which can download them again. Models you added by hand won't come back.

rules.title: JetBrains IDEs — version caches
rules.description: Indexes and caches for each JetBrains IDE version (~/.cache/JetBrains). Folders for versions you no longer use stay behind after every upgrade. Skipped while a JetBrains IDE or Android Studio is open.
rules.comeback: The IDE rebuilds its indexes the next time it opens a project. Your settings live elsewhere and are not touched.

rules.title: Playwright — browser builds
rules.description: Chromium, Firefox and WebKit builds Playwright downloaded for testing (~/.cache/ms-playwright). Each Playwright upgrade adds new ones.
rules.comeback: Run: npx playwright install — it downloads the versions your project needs.

rules.title: Puppeteer — browser builds
rules.description: Chrome builds Puppeteer downloaded when it was installed (~/.cache/puppeteer).
rules.comeback: Run: npx puppeteer browsers install chrome — or reinstall the package.

rules.title: Cypress — app binaries
rules.description: Cypress app versions downloaded by your projects (~/.cache/Cypress). Old versions are never removed on their own.
rules.comeback: Run: npx cypress install — it downloads the version a project needs.

rules.title: Electron — download cache
rules.description: Electron releases downloaded when installing Electron apps you are developing (~/.cache/electron).
rules.comeback: Downloaded again the next time a project installs Electron.

rules.title: Yarn — package cache
rules.description: Packages Yarn has downloaded (~/.cache/yarn and ~/.yarn/berry/cache). Re-fetched on the next install.
rules.comeback: Yarn fetches packages again on the next install.

rules.title: pnpm — package store
rules.description: pnpm's shared package store (~/.local/share/pnpm/store). Your projects' node_modules folders are hard links into it, so clearing it frees almost nothing until those projects are cleaned too — pnpm's own prune command is the safe way to shrink it, which is why this starts unchecked.
rules.comeback: Run: pnpm store prune — it removes only packages no project uses.

rules.title: Bun — install cache
rules.description: Packages Bun has downloaded (~/.bun/install/cache). Re-fetched on the next install.
rules.comeback: Bun downloads packages again on the next install.

rules.title: Deno — module cache
rules.description: Remote modules and compiled code Deno has cached (~/.cache/deno). Re-fetched when a script needs them.
rules.comeback: Deno downloads and compiles modules again when a script needs them.

rules.title: node-gyp — headers
rules.description: Node.js headers downloaded to compile native add-ons (~/.cache/node-gyp).
rules.comeback: node-gyp downloads the headers again the next time a native package builds.

rules.title: Go — module cache
rules.description: Go's downloaded module cache (~/go/pkg/mod). Moved to Trash as one restorable folder; modules are re-downloaded when needed.
rules.comeback: The go command downloads modules again when a build needs them.

rules.title: ccache — compiler cache
rules.description: Compiled C and C++ objects ccache keeps so rebuilding the same code is instant (~/.cache/ccache, ~/.ccache).
rules.comeback: ccache fills it again as you compile. The first builds afterwards are slower.

rules.title: sccache — compiler cache
rules.description: Compiled Rust, C and C++ output sccache keeps on disk (~/.cache/sccache). Skipped while the sccache server is running.
rules.comeback: sccache fills it again as you compile. The first builds afterwards are slower.

rules.title: Composer — package cache
rules.description: PHP packages Composer has downloaded (~/.cache/composer, ~/.composer/cache). Re-downloaded when an install needs them.
rules.comeback: Composer downloads packages again when an install needs them.

rules.title: NuGet — global packages
rules.description: Every NuGet package your .NET projects have restored (~/.nuget/packages).
rules.comeback: Run: dotnet restore — it downloads the packages a project needs again.

rules.title: NuGet — HTTP cache
rules.description: Package feeds and downloads NuGet keeps to make restores faster (~/.local/share/NuGet/v3-cache, http-cache).
rules.comeback: NuGet downloads what it needs again on the next restore.

rules.title: Dart / Flutter — pub cache
rules.description: Dart and Flutter packages downloaded by pub (~/.pub-cache). Re-downloaded by the next pub get.
rules.comeback: Run: dart pub get or flutter pub get — they download the packages again.

rules.title: uv — package cache
rules.description: Packages, wheels and Python builds uv has downloaded (~/.cache/uv). Re-downloaded on the next sync or install.
rules.comeback: uv downloads what it needs again on the next sync or install.

rules.title: Poetry — package cache
rules.description: Package metadata and downloaded files Poetry keeps between installs (~/.cache/pypoetry). Re-downloaded on the next install.
rules.comeback: Poetry downloads them again on the next install.

rules.title: VS Code / Cursor — code caches
rules.description: Compiled code cache and copies of extension installers for VS Code and Cursor (~/.config/Code and ~/.config/Cursor: CachedData, CachedExtensionVSIXs, Cache). These folders are not documented by Microsoft, so this starts unchecked.
rules.comeback: VS Code and Cursor rebuild their caches as you use them.

rules.title: Flatpak — unused runtimes
rules.description: Runs 'flatpak uninstall --unused -y' — removes Flatpak runtimes and extensions no installed app uses anymore (they pile up after updates). Apps and their data are never touched; never delete Flatpak folders by hand. Disabled by default: set "enabled": true on this rule after reviewing.
rules.comeback: An app that later needs a removed runtime downloads it again on its next launch.

rules.title: Docker — build cache
rules.description: Runs 'docker builder prune -f' — removes Docker's build cache only (the layers docker build compiled and stored). Images, containers and volumes are never touched. Disabled by default: set "enabled": true on this rule after reviewing.
rules.comeback: Docker rebuilds the cache the next time you build the same images — the first build afterwards is slower.
